To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

elderly listeners with hearing impairment, with and without hearing-aid use, are able to use visual speech information for lexical tone perception, but the use of visual speech does not differ significantly between the two groups.

the HI group, with or without hearing aids, performed worse than the NH group on auditory-visual and auditory-only tone discrimination, that there was slightly more visual enhancement for the HI group than the NH group, but this difference was not statistically significant, and that there was a different ranking of relative difficulty of the tone contrasts for the NH group compared to the HI group, whether with hearing aids or not.

the elderly Thai Hearing Impaired with and without hearing devices can use visual speech information for tone discrimination, but do so similarly, not significantly more enhanced, than the elderly Thai with normal hearing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the perception of lexical tone by Thai elderly with and without HI, the effects of visual augmentation of tone perception, and the effects of hearing aids.
the use of the auditory and visual cues for the perception of lexical tone by Thai listeners.
the effects of aging on the perception of lexical tone.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the elderly Hearing Impaired Thais, with and without hearing aid, can and do use visual speech information in lexical tone perception.
the HI group, both with and without hearing aid, use visual cues to augment their perception of tone in a similar way to the NH elderly.
the Hearing Impairment in elderly Thais has little or no effect on their perception of lexical tone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hearing loss in the elderly results in poorer auditory perception of Thai tones, but does not lead to greater reliance on visual information for lexical tone perception.

the elderly Thai with hearing impairment, with or without hearing aids, can and do use visual speech information, but they do not use visual speech information in a more enhanced manner than their normal hearing counterparts.
visual speech information can be used to facilitate lexical tone perception in the elderly, regardless of whether they have hearing loss or not.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the elderly Hearing Impaired with and without hearing devices use the visual modality to augment tone perception.
elderly listeners can and do use visual information to enhance their perception of lexical tones, even when they have severe hearing impairment.

elderly Thai speakers of Thai with hearing loss can benefit from the use of Hearing Aids, but also from visual cues, and that visual cues are used by all Thai elderly, regardless of their hearing status.
